# Security Policy

## Supported Versions

Currently, UniSphere is in active development. All work happens off the `dev-branch`. Only the latest deployed production release and the active main tree receive security patches.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

If you discover a security vulnerability within UniSphere (for example, related to RBAC escalation, token leaks, or data exposure between university scopes), **do not create a public issue**. 

Instead, please privately report it to the **CHARUSAT Development Club** lead maintainers (or Team 1 Core Leads).

When reporting, please include:
* A detailed description of the vulnerability and its potential impact on the platform.
* Step-by-step instructions (or a script) to reproduce the issue locally or in staging.
* Potential fixes or mitigations if you have identified them.

We take the security of this multi-tier university platform very seriously and will work with you to patch any critical flaws before disclosure.
